To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) Q*BERT, a question answering agent, outperforms the state-of-the-art by a factor of 2.5 on nine text games and (ii) MC!Q*BERt, a question answering, knowledge graph building, and bottleneck overcoming agent, outperformed Q*BERT and the state-of-the art by a factor of up to 3.5 on nine games.
(a) Q*BERT learns to build a world knowledge graph by answering questions, and (b) MC!Q*BERt learns a sequence of policy modules to efficiently overcome bottlenecks.

(1) a Q*BERT agent that builds a knowledge graph of a textual game is able to overcome bottleneks in the environment, and that (2) a MC!Q*BER that uses an intrinsic motivation to detect and overcome bottlenecks is able to outperform the current state-of the-art in the text game domain.
